XXV.}}</noinclude>ye forth to meete him. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=7}}† Then arose al those virgins: and they trimmed their lampes. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=8}}† And the foolish said to the vvise, Giue vs of {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ If we be not in the fauour of God, and haue not our owne merites, we shal not be holpen by other mens deserts at the day of iudgement.}}∷ your oile: because our lampes are going out. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=9}}† The vvise ansvvered, saying, Lest peraduenture there suffise not for vs and you, goe rather to them that sel: and bie for your selues. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=10}}† And vvhiles they vvent to bie, the bridegrome vvas come: and they that vvere ready, entred vvith him to the mariage, and the gate vvas shut. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=11}}† But last of al come also the other virgins, saying: Lord, Lord, open to vs. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=12}}† But he ansvvering said, Amen I say to you, I knovv you not. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=13}}† Watch ye therfore, because you knovv not the day nor the houre.⊣

{{verse|chapter=25|verse=14}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for a Cōfessor that is a Bishop.}}For {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 19, 12.''}}* euen as a man going into a strange countrie, called his seruants, and deliuered them his goods. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=15}}† And to one he gaue fiue talents, and to an other tvvo, and to an other one, to euery one according to his propre facultie: and immediatly he tooke his iourney. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=16}}† And he that had receiued the fiue talents, vvent his vvay, and occupied vvith the same, and gained other fiue. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=17}}† Likevvise also he that had receiued the tvvo, gained other tvvo. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=18}}† But he that had receiued the one, going his vvay digged into the earth, and hid his lords money. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=19}}† But after much time the lord of those seruants commeth, and made a count vvith them. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=20}}† And there came he that had receiued the fiue talents, and offred other fiue talents, saying, Lord fiue talents thou didst deliuer me, behold {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Free will with Gods grace doth merite.}}∷ I haue gained other fiue besides. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=21}}† His lord said vnto him: Wel fare thee good and faithful seruant, because thou hast been faithful ouer a fevv things, I vvil place thee ouer many things: enter into the ioy of thy lord. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=22}}† And there came also he that had receiued the tvvo talents, and said, Lord tvvo talents thou didst deliuer me: behold I haue gained other tvvo. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=23}}† His lord said to him, Wel fare thee good and faithful seruant: because thou hast been faithful ouer a fevv things, I vvil place thee ouer many things, enter into the ioy of thy lord.⊣ {{verse|chapter=25|verse=24}}† And he also that had receiued the one talent, came forth, and said, Lord, I knovv that thou art a hard man, thou reapest vvhere thou didst not sovv: and gatherest vvhere thou strawedst not: {{verse|chapter=25|verse=25}}† and being afraid I vvent, and hid thy talent in the earth: behold loe here thou hast that vvhich thine is. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=26}}† And his lord ansvvering, said to him: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ A terrible example for al such as do not employ the very least gift of God, to his glorie.}}∷ Naughtie and sloughtful seruant, thou didst knovv that I reape vvhere<noinclude>{{rh|||I}}</noinclude>
